llm.summary: This is a teacher-facing Chinese K12 chemistry lesson-planning skill with scoped classroom-data use and clear safety/privacy limits.

dimensions.detail: It relies on platform memory/file capabilities and classWorkspace data, but the schema limits reads and writes to class profile, weak points, tiers, logs, review plans, and lessonPlans.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is markdown, references, and a JSON schema; no executable scripts, remote payload retrieval, dependency installation, or tool replacement behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation is limited to chemistry lesson design, with explicit handoffs for lab procedures, notation drills, exams, and other subjects; crisis and student-facing boundaries are disclosed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It can generate lesson-plan entries for persistence, but they are described as teacher-confirmed pending entries and the skill provides view, correction, deletion, pause, export, and sharing controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently support chemistry lesson-plan drafting, curriculum alignment, three-representation pedagogy, and high-level experiment placement rather than executable lab procedures.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this for Chinese-language chemistry teachers working in mainland China K12 curriculum contexts. Do not use it unchanged for other regions or languages unless the operator localizes curriculum assumptions, safety contacts, and minor-data rules; teachers should still verify lesson plans, generated materials, and all experiment safety decisions before classroom use.
llm.findings:
[AE4] expected: The flagged Unicode/mixed-script content appears to be ordinary Chinese curriculum markdown and punctuation; inspection found no hidden control characters, obfuscated instructions, secrets, or executable payloads.
[SQP-3] expected: The China-mainland Chinese K12 assumptions are explicit in shared/platform-conventions.md, including instructions to localize crisis contacts, curriculum, and legal defaults before use outside that context.
[aig-skill-scan] expected: The supplied SARIF reported no results, and local inspection did not find instruction hijacking, persistence backdoors, remote execution, privilege escalation, or tool spoofing.
